title: Story of Scaling Decentralized Open Hardware
description: In 2020, with supply chains frozen by India’s lockdown, Maker’s Asylum’s M19 Initiative produced over 1 million face shields in 49 days. Not from one factory, but through a network of independent makers and small fabricators building from an open design. This talk is a field report on what made that scale possible: a design simple enough to reproduce anywhere, local nodes free to fork and adapt it, lightweight quality checks without central control, and coordination with almost no formal structure. I’ll also share where it strained and what we’d design differently. These lessons speak directly to questions the Ethereum community is facing now: how decentralized networks coordinate under pressure, how public goods get funded and sustained, and why local resilience depends on hardware being open too.
abstract: How did a community makerspace coordinate more than a million face shields in 49 days during India’s 2020 lockdown, without a factory or a central command? This lightning talk unpacks the M19 Initiative as a case study in decentralized open hardware, leaving attendees with practical patterns for coordinating local production networks under pressure, and the failure modes to design around.
